newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Iran denies its forces are in northern Iraq - radio.
newsitem.headline: Iran denies its forces are in northern Iraq - radio.

text.p: Iran has denied that its military forces are present in northern Iraq, where rival Kurdish groups are battling for control of the region, Tehran Radio said on Friday.

Baghdad and Iraq's Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), whose joint attack on the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) led to retaliatory U.S. missile strikes on Iraq this week, charge that Iranian forces help the PUK.
Tehran Radio, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation, said Iran's embassy in Bonn had issued a statement denying that Iranian forces were in Iraq.
Iran had previously denied that it forces were involved in the latest fighting in northern Iraq but the embassy statement was the first time Iran said it had no forces there.
Iran, which fought a war with Iraq from 1980 to 1988, sent troops into northern Iraq in July to strike at Iranian Kurdish rebel groups based there.
President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani this week rejected charges of meddling in northern Iraq and said Iranian operations were aimed only at anti-Tehran guerrillas.
The Iranian statement in Bonn was in response to a German Foreign Ministry statement on Monday that alleged Iranian troops were present in northern Iraq.
